title: Sequence-aware quantization benchmarking and calibration stress harness
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Build a reproducible stress-harness that evaluates throughput and latency for FP8 and INT8 quantized variants under mixed-sequence-length traffic and realistic batching policies. We want sequence-aware batching and calibration checks that expose failure modes missed by fixed-length runs (KV-cache warmup, tail latency during long-context bursts, quant scale saturation on early vs late tokens). Deliverables: 1) benchmark harness and config matrix 2) calibration reservoir + per-layer scale heatmaps 3) accuracy validation report (perplexity delta, embedding similarity, generation regression checks) 4) recommendations for default quant profile fallbacks and SLO guardrails.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Harness runs reproducibly on dev cluster and on perf staging (results within 5% between runs). 2) Generate a 12-cell matrix (FP8/INT8 x 3 calibration strategies x 2 batching policies) with p50/p95/p99 latencies, RPS, tokens/sec, and memory. 3) Produce an accuracy validation summary with statistically-significant comparisons (Wilcoxon or paired t-test) of perplexity and 512-token generation similarity. 4) Document a safe default quant profile and suggested fallback policy when accuracy drift exceeds threshold.
experiment_matrix: Model variants: open-7B & open-13B. Quant modes: FP8 dynamic, FP8 static-calib, INT8 per-channel. Calibration strategies: reservoir-sample (mixed-length), layerwise-min-max, layerwise-statistic-based (kl/divergence). Batching policies: sequence-aware rolling-batcher (limits collated seq-length within batch), fixed-window batcher (pad-to-max in window). Traffic patterns: steady short (avg 32), mixed (20/128/512 split 60/30/10), long-burst (single 2048 spike every 60s). Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, GPU memory, QoR metrics: perplexity delta, embedding cosine similarity on reference prompts, top-k token distribution KL against FP32 baseline.
harness_infrastructure: Perf staging cluster: 4x A100-80GB nodes (NCCL), 2x ND96 (for A10-like runs) on cloud-region eu-west-1. Runtime: runtime-1.22 candidate build with dynamic-kernel-selection flag enabled. Collector: prometheus + perf-trace flow (per-request spans) + token-level cost emitter. Synthetic traffic: trafgen v2 with jitter injection to simulate arrival skew.
calibration_plan: 1) Collect representative tokens with reservoir sampling capped at 100k tokens per run. 2) Generate per-layer scale candidates using min-max and 99.9th percentile heuristics. 3) For FP8 dynamic, run short warmups to collect scale drift across sequence positions (token index heatmap). 4) For INT8, collect per-channel weight activation histograms and compute symmetric/asymmetric scales. 5) Save calibration artifacts (json heatmaps + binary hist files) to /perf/artifacts/quant-calib/2026-03-10.
validation_criteria: Accuracy pass if: perplexity increase <= 1.5% over FP32 baseline AND mean embedding cosine similarity >= 0.985 on eval prompt set (n=500). Additionally, generation regression detected via delta in top-5 token mass must be <0.02 average. If metrics fail, mark profile unstable and recommend fallback to FP16 or different calibration strategy.
initial_results_summary: Early runs (open-7B) show FP8-dynamic maintains p50 parity with FP32 for mixed traffic but exhibits p99 spikes +22% when long-burst sequences are admitted into batched contexts without KV-warmup. INT8 per-channel reduces memory by ~18% vs FP8 but shows a consistent perplexity delta of +2.1% under layerwise-min-max calibration on long-context prompts. Reservoir-sample calibration reduced INT8 perplexity delta to +0.9% while adding ~8% calibration time. Sequence-aware batching reduced p99 tail by 35% in mixed traffic compared to naive pad-to-max batching.
run_steps: 1) Provision perf staging cluster with runtime-1.22-candidate image
2) Upload calibration seed corpus (5000 prompts) to s3 bucket and warm GPU cache
3) Launch calibration collector with reservoir sampling enabled (100k token cap)
4) Generate quant profiles for FP8 and INT8 variants and register as candidate models
5) Run benchmark matrix: 3 repeats per cell with varied RNG seeds and jitter settings
6) Collect metrics, aggregate token-level traces and compute QoR comparisons vs FP32 baseline
7) Run statistical tests and populate perf dashboard
8) Summarize results and open follow-up tickets for unstable profiles
